title: Grade 6 Science — Tue, May 26
description: Components of Food — Day 2 of 5: Testing for nutrients
subject: science

questions.question: Which reagent is used to test for starch in food?
questions.explanation: Iodine solution turns blue-black in the presence of starch. This is the standard starch test.

questions.question: A food sample is tested with iodine solution. It turns blue-black. This means:
questions.explanation: Blue-black colour with iodine confirms the presence of starch.

questions.question: To test for fat in a food sample, you rub it on paper. A positive result shows:
options: A translucent (greasy) spot on the paper
questions.explanation: Fats leave a translucent (see-through) greasy spot on paper — this is the paper spot test for fats.

questions.question: The Biuret test (using copper sulphate and sodium hydroxide) is used to detect:
questions.explanation: Biuret reagent turns violet/purple in the presence of proteins — it tests for peptide bonds.

questions.question: Which food would test POSITIVE for starch using iodine?
questions.explanation: Potato is rich in starch. Mashed potato would turn blue-black with iodine.

questions.question: What colour does Benedict's solution turn when reducing sugar (like glucose) is present?
questions.explanation: Benedict's test is used for reducing sugars. Positive result ranges from green → yellow → brick-red depending on sugar concentration.

questions.question: Which food would leave a greasy spot on paper (positive fat test)?
questions.explanation: Groundnuts are rich in fat/oil. They would leave a clear greasy spot on paper.

questions.question: In a food test experiment, why do we need a control (untested paper/water)?
options: To compare results and confirm the test is working correctly
questions.explanation: A control lets us compare what the result looks like WITHOUT the nutrient, so we can be sure our positive result is genuine.

questions.question: Which nutrient would you expect to find in ghee using the paper spot test?
questions.explanation: Ghee is almost pure fat. Rubbing it on paper will leave a large translucent greasy spot.

questions.question: Vitamin C can be tested using which reagent (DCPIP)?
options: DCPIP turns blue when Vitamin C is present
DCPIP turns colourless (from blue) when Vitamin C is present
DCPIP turns red with Vitamin C
DCPIP has no reaction with Vitamin C
questions.explanation: DCPIP (blue) is decolourised to colourless by Vitamin C — this indicates presence of Vitamin C.

questions.question: To test for protein in egg white, you would use:
questions.explanation: Biuret reagent is the correct test for protein. Egg white (albumin) would turn the solution purple.

questions.question: If food shows a negative iodine test, it means:
options: The food has lots of starch
questions.explanation: A negative result (iodine stays brown/yellow) means no starch is present in the food sample.

questions.question: Which of these would likely test POSITIVE for protein?
questions.explanation: Milk contains casein protein. Biuret test on milk would give a violet colour.

questions.question: Why do we test different food samples for nutrients?
options: To find out which nutrients are present and plan a balanced diet
To check if food is cooked properly
questions.explanation: Nutrient tests help us understand the composition of food so we can plan a balanced diet with all required nutrients.

questions.question: A food sample turns blue-black with iodine AND leaves a greasy spot. This food contains:
questions.explanation: Blue-black with iodine = starch present. Greasy spot on paper = fat present. The food contains both.
